current_events: American troops complete their withdrawal from Iraq, ending their 23-year presence in the country that started with the 2003 U.S. invasion, and also the 12-year U.S. intervention against the Islamic State in Iraq and Syria
Withdrawal of United States troops from Iraq

A United States federal judge approves media conglomerate Paramount Skydance's settlement with 12 states that challenged its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery on antitrust grounds, allowing the $81 billion merger to proceed toward completion
Proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery by Paramount Skydance
A helicopter crashes in Marondera, Zimbabwe, killing all six people on board, including businessman Wicknell Chivayo and his wife

The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit halts Christa Pike's execution in Tennessee shortly before it was scheduled, to allow for further review of whether evidence of childhood sexual abuse was adequately considered at sentencing; the U.S. Supreme Court shortly after lifts the Sixth Circuit's stay order, allowing the execution to proceed
Pike is sent to a hospital following the failed administration of two rounds of the drugs used to perform the lethal injection
Capital punishment in the United States

A Turkish court orders the closure of independent news website T24 and its social media accounts after the justice ministry reported that the outlet had published 118 items during the previous year which the court classified as "LGBTQ propaganda"
2026 Turkish LGBTQ raids, Censorship in Turkey, Censorship of LGBTQ issues

A Flydubai flight from Dubai, United Arab Emirates, to Tel Aviv, Israel, is landed safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, by a relief crew after the copilot violently attacked the captain in an attempted aircraft hijacking

Romania's parliament rejects prime minister-designate Siegfried Mureșan's proposed government, receiving 182 of the 233 votes required for approval, prolonging the political crisis that began after Ilie Bolojan's government fell in May
At least 450 people are arrested and 76 people are injured after schools students in France protest over class overcrowding and teacher shortages

The Tokyo District Court rules that a person's voice can receive protection under publicity rights, in Japan's first case involving alleged audio deepfake, while dismissing actor Kenjiro Tsuda's request to remove already-deleted TikTok videos
